title: Zoom in: a message is ready, leased, acked, retried or parked
caption: The broker deletes a message only on ack; every failure path leads back to ready or to the dead-letter queue.

steps.text: The message is published and waits in the ready state.
A worker receives it. The broker doesn't delete it; it leases it: the message is invisible to other workers for 30 s.
The worker charges the card, sending the order id as the provider's idempotency key.
Success: the worker acks, and only then is the message deleted. Ack after the effect, never before.

scenarios.name: Provider times out
scenarios.summary: A transient error is retried later, not immediately, so a struggling provider isn't hammered while it recovers.

steps.text: The charge times out after 3 s.
The worker nacks with a delay: retry in 10 s, plus random jitter so a thousand failures don't all return at the same instant.
When the delay is due the message is ready again, with its attempt count raised to 2.
The second attempt succeeds. If the first charge had actually gone through, the same key makes the provider return that result instead of charging again.

scenarios.name: Worker crashes
scenarios.summary: No ack means no delete: the lease runs out and the message comes back by itself. At-least-once delivery, so handlers must be idempotent.

steps.text: The worker receives the message and is killed mid-charge (out of memory).
Nobody acks. After 30 s the lease expires and the broker makes the message ready again.
Another worker picks it up and charges with the same key: the customer is charged once.

scenarios.name: Poison message
scenarios.summary: A message that can never succeed is moved aside after N attempts, so it costs five tries and an alert instead of an endless loop.

steps.text: An order carries a malformed currency code: the handler throws every time.
Each failure returns it via the retry scheduler; the attempt count climbs.
At attempt 6 the broker moves it to the dead-letter queue instead of delivering it again. The rest of the queue keeps flowing.
An engineer inspects it, ships the fix, and the redrive tool sends it back to the ready queue.
